consolidatedFindings.title: The claimEnabled gate is fully bypassable in two ordinary transactions: withdraw books the whole reward ungated, then autoAnnihilate with zero principal mints 100% of the backlog raw

sources.contribution: Mechanical derivation of the two-transaction path and the arithmetic collapse; the falsified story-025 headline claim ('autoAnnihilate becomes the only reward path') and the falsified Auditor-Note rationale; the observation that it works while Antimatter itself is PAUSED (the `if (annihilatable > 0)` block is skipped and Antimatter.mint is not whenNotPaused); free on the wired direct ERC4626YieldStrategy (no round-trip haircut); impactBound (no over-emission, owed is exactly conserved).

Independent confirmation that claimEnabled is read at exactly ONE site (:440) and therefore gates claim() only; evidence lines :540/:542/:596/:605. Explicit warning carried forward VERBATIM: the pattern's OWN harm (over-mint) does NOT apply and must not be claimed.

consolidatedFindings.title: The exit-shortfall floor is blind to a fee-charging ERC4626 vault: the allowance is 2 raw units + 1 bp while the shortfall is proportional, so an external Tokemak fee crossing 1.00 bp bricks the only reward path

escalationTrigger.condition: The wired autopool's modeled exit discount f exceeds EXACTLY 1.00 bp (EXIT_ROUNDING_ALLOWANCE_BPS). Above that, every autoAnnihilate above N = 2/(f - 1e-4) raw units reverts 'StableStaker: exit shortfall'.
escalationTrigger.howToMonitor: Re-run reports/stable-staker/17/poc/Run17_ECON001_ExitFeeBrick.t.sol::test_measure_autopool_exit_haircut_bps against the live autopools. It is a pure measurement test and needs no protocol state.
escalationTrigger.whyLowToday: The trigger has NOT fired. See refutation below.

sources.contribution: The quantified derivation: netFloor == gross == netWanted via AYieldStrategy's capped identity (previewExitFor NOT overridden by ERC4626YieldStrategy); pass condition N*(f - 1e-4) <= 2; the DECIMALS CLIFF (the flat 2-unit allowance is worth 2e-6 USDC on a 6-decimal pool but 2e-18 DOLA on an 18-decimal pool, so on an 18-decimal pool the ENTIRE margin is the 1 bp); both allowances are `constant` with NO setter, so there is no parameter remedy.

The Law-2 half. story-025's own Review Failure Report 2026-08-31 (blocking [high]) demanded: 'Re-derive the shortfall floor so a double-rounded-down ERC4626 delivery of amount - 1 (or a routine haircut) does not revert autoAnnihilate.' Round 3 satisfies the ROUNDING-scale criterion only, and Autonomous Decision 1 explicitly DEFERS the fee case to a previewExitFor override in vault-RM that does not exist at the pinned commit cdd0743. The round-3 regression fixture (MockERC4626Vault = OZ reference + donation hook) charges NO fee, so it is structurally incapable of detecting the residual.

The allowance-sizing sub-observation: netFloor = (netQuote * gross)/grossQuote linearly rescales a floor the market strategy computes non-linearly. MR-17-01 asked for a Tier-3 bound because 'two floors cost at most 2 units' was ASSERTED from source, not proven. THAT BOUND NOW EXISTS -- see resolvedBy. MR-17-01 is NOT a separate finding and is NOT the Linear-Depletion family class (the error is O(1) absolute, not a rate drift); it is retained here as evidence of why the flat allowance is load-bearing.

consolidatedFindings.rootCause: EXIT_ROUNDING_ALLOWANCE (2 raw units, :70) + EXIT_ROUNDING_ALLOWANCE_BPS (1 bp, :78) are sized in ROUNDING units, but the shortfall an ERC4626 exit fee produces is PROPORTIONAL to the exit size. Both are `constant` with no setter.

instances.role: capped identity, not overridden by ERC4626YieldStrategy -- the reason netFloor collapses to netWanted

whyTwoEntriesNotOne: DIFFERENT ROOT CAUSE. DEDUP-002 is PROPORTIONAL fee-blindness (an allowance sized in rounding units against a shortfall that scales with size). DEDUP-003 is an INTEGER double round-down at the bottom of the range (convertToShares(1) == 0 at any share price > 1). They fail at opposite ends of the size axis.
DIFFERENT TRIGGER. DEDUP-002 requires an EXTERNAL Tokemak parameter to cross 1 bp -- it has not, and is not live. DEDUP-003 requires nothing external and was OBSERVED HAPPENING at HEAD, 50 times.

DIFFERENT REMEDY. DEDUP-002 wants a fee-aware previewExitFor override in reflax-yield-vault. DEDUP-003 wants a dust short-circuit or a zero-shares pre-check in StableStakerV2; the flat allowance must NOT be raised for it because raising it is the wrong lever and lowering it breaks the scaling law.

DIFFERENT EVIDENCE STATUS. Merging would let the live, observed dust revert inherit DEDUP-002's REFUTED framing, or let the refuted fee-brick inherit DEDUP-003's 'observed at HEAD' credibility. Either direction is a misreport. Keeping them apart is the only honest option.
consolidatedFindings.rootCause: Against the real ERC4626YieldStrategy over a yielded vault, netWanted == 1 gives convertToShares(1) == 0 in _disposeShares (ERC4626YieldStrategy.sol:126-138), the redeem delivers 0 assets, and require(received > 0 && ...) at :588-589 reverts.

evidencePreserved.observedRate: 50 / 17,729 gate-closed attempts = 0.28%. 46 of the 50 landed on pool 1 (the REAL ERC4626YieldStrategy over a real OZ vault) and 0 on the idle pool.
evidencePreserved.loadBearing: LOAD-BEARING. The fixtureCaveats explicitly state that the FEE conclusions are not load-bearing (MockERC4626Vault charges no exit fee) but the ROUNDING conclusions ARE, because they come from the real ERC4626YieldStrategy over a real OZ vault. The 4 pool-2 hits (honest market strategy, laxer than a real AMM) are NOT load-bearing and are discounted here.
evidencePreserved.selfHealing: Yes -- the condition clears after further accrual pushes owed above the dust boundary. This is a TRANSIENT liveness failure, not a permanent brick. That is the main reason it stays Low.
evidencePreserved.scalingLaw: The double round-down loses up to one share's worth of assets while the allowance is 2 + netFloor/10_000, so the floor fails whenever assetsPerShare > 2 + netFloor/10_000. Demonstrated at an UNREALISTIC 1247 assets/share in test_scalingLaw_highSharePriceBreaksTheFloorForOrdinaryExits. NOT a live finding at stablecoin-autopool prices -- but it is why EXIT_ROUNDING_ALLOWANCE = 2 is load-bearing and must not be reduced.
evidencePreserved.diagnosticHarm: The revert message accuses an HONEST strategy of lying. Combined with DEDUP-002's remedy note and DEDUP-010's false-green view, an operator debugging this is pointed at the wrong contract three times over.

consolidatedFindings.PRESERVED_AS_DISTINCT: Explicitly NOT merged with DEDUP-001. DEDUP-001 is the gate being TOO OPEN (bypassable). DEDUP-004 is the gate being TOO CLOSED (in a state where it removes the last recoverable path). Same flag, opposite failure directions, opposite remedies. Collapsing them would hide one of the two.

evidencePreserved.measuredDestruction: Tier-3 measured 4166666666666666650000 wei of Antimatter entitlement destroyed on the emergencyWithdraw path.
evidencePreserved.whyItIsNEW: Before story-025 this trap did NOT exist: claim() was ungated, so a trapped staker could claim first and THEN emergencyWithdraw. The gate is precisely what converts a recoverable situation into a forced forfeiture.
evidencePreserved.v2Premise: Under the V2 premise (Antimatter is redeemable 1:1 into unbacked phUSD via the permissionless Antimatter.annihilate), the destroyed backlog is real user value, NOT opportunity cost. The project-wide minter-cushion / externally-derived-yield suppressions are VOID for V2 (ledger lastRunSummary, run-16, story-023).
evidencePreserved.raceDynamic: The buffer is first-come-first-served (_routeExit:1188). story-025 adds REWARD-seeking callers to a queue that previously held only PRINCIPAL-seeking callers, so the buffer is exhausted sooner and the trap closes on later stakers first. Front-running another staker's autoAnnihilate to take the last of the buffer at par is profitable, because the buffer pays par on a below-par position.
evidencePreserved.expectedNotExotic: The idle buffer is WORKING CAPITAL, not a solvency reserve (project standing concept). A buffer smaller than a given staker's gross request is the EXPECTED state at scale, not an edge case.

consolidatedFindings.footgunLaw3: Yes. CLAUDE.md anticipates exactly this class for the ANTIMATTER PAUSE ('the owner flips claimEnabled to true for the duration of any antimatter pause') but does NOT anticipate it for the UNDERWATER case -- so the operational obligation the design depends on is unwritten for the condition most likely to occur.
consolidatedFindings.remedy: (a) exempt the reward-only leg from the underwater guard (a caller whose netWanted is 0 moves no principal and should not be blocked); or (b) extend the CLAUDE.md two-pause-deadlock obligation to cover 'any wired strategy underwater'; or (c) have emergencyWithdraw PRESERVE unclaimedReward rather than zero it.

consolidatedFindings.title: autoAnnihilate draws the tolerance-inflated GROSS from the shared underwater buffer per unit of reward -- a known wont-fix class reaching new code, disclosed for its RATE, not re-filed on its merits

sources.contribution: The disclosure itself, the prior-entry lookup, and the honest weakness of the re-file basis.

Quantification: excess buffer drawn = netWanted * slip / (MAX_BPS - slip) per call; at slip = 200 bps and a 100 USDC reward, 2.04 USDC of extra buffer. Socialised-loss formula. Proof it is NOT amplifiable by splitting into many calls.
The original observation.

MEASURED: 202767365267183752539 raw units (202.77 DAI2) paid to ONE caller as `surplus` out of the SHARED idle buffer in a SINGLE autoAnnihilate, at 1.5% exit slippage with the strategy 2% below par. The underwater buffer carve-out at :1190 was reached 6,387 times across the two campaigns.

consolidatedFindings.rootCause: _routeExit's underwater branch (:1186-1195) returns `gross` VERBATIM without measuring, and calls relinquishPrincipal(token, gross) which moves zero assets and only writes clientBalances down. With a market strategy gross = ceilDiv(netWanted * MAX_BPS, MAX_BPS - slip) > netWanted, so surplus = gross - netWanted is transferred to the caller at :609 out of the shared buffer.

priorLedgerEntriesNAMED.title: Underwater withdraw buffer is FCFS at par, socializing strategy loss onto slow stakers

consolidatedFindings.title: autoAnnihilateAvailable returns true in exactly the state where autoAnnihilate reverts, inverting the story's own Decision-4 rationale -- and its probe is near-vacuous

sources.contribution: The Law-2 inversion. story-025 Round-2 Decision 4 reasons that returning FALSE would be the inconsistent answer; the code makes TRUE the inconsistent answer. The view early-returns true whenever strategy.principalOf(token, address(this)) == 0, but a staker can hold user.amount > 0 in that state (principal idle after a buffer-path relinquishPrincipal, or a strategy set before deposits route into it). Both previewExitFor implementations cap grossToRequest at clientBalances, so grossQuote == 0 and :557 reverts 'StableStaker: exit unavailable'.

MERGED HALF: 'the finding that survives is HONESTY OF THE VIEW, not extraction' -- autoAnnihilateAvailable(token) returning true does not mean autoAnnihilate(token) will succeed, and the UI it was written for will show a live button on a pool where every call reverts. Plus the vacuity proof: for the DIRECT strategy previewExitFor(1) returns min(1, clientBalances) and clientBalances >= 1 is ALREADY guaranteed by the principalOf != 0 early-return at :1058, so the strategy leg is a TAUTOLOGY; for the MARKET strategy ceilDiv(1*MAX_BPS, MAX_BPS - slip) == 1 for any slip < 5000 bps. The view detects exactly ONE condition: a 100% slippage tolerance. The OTHER half of ECON-007 ('is the probe a free option?' -> NO) is a negative result and is parked, not filed.

consolidatedFindings.rootCause: The availability view's preconditions do not match the transaction's preconditions in either direction: it early-returns true on principalOf == 0 (F-03), and its 1-unit probe cannot detect a capped real quote or a fee-charging vault (ECON-007).

specVsActual.spec: story-025 round-2 'The agreed design' item 2 + front-running analysis: 'It is bounded: ERC4626MarketYieldStrategy enforces minOut = idealUnderlying * (MAX_BPS - slippageToleranceBps) / MAX_BPS internally and reverts before autoAnnihilate ever sees the proceeds, so the extractable amount is capped at the tolerance...'
specVsActual.actual: A SECOND, unmodelled cap exists: both previewExitFor implementations cap grossToRequest at clientBalances[token][address(this)]. When it binds, grossQuote, gross, netFloor and netUsed all shrink below netWanted and the remainder is minted raw via excess = excessBase + (netWanted - netUsed) * scale (:596). On ERC4626MarketYieldStrategy the cap binds STRUCTURALLY, because _acquireShares books the haircut creditedPrincipal rather than the nominal deposit, so clientBalances is PERMANENTLY below the pool's nominal totalStaked.

consolidatedFindings.notAValueLeak: Conservation still holds -- owed in equals annihilated + raw-minted + carried dust (independently verified by ECON-005 and INV-1/INV-2). No Antimatter is created beyond what the caller was owed. The second cap is protocol-level, NOT caller-set, so it is not an attack vector. Documentation fix, not a code fix.
